headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading error: next-ai-draw-io’s broad egress/MCP can expose content while ai-engineering-hub provides no blocking controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io uses MCP and natural-language tool use, so prompt-like content can influence actions if fed into its workflow. ai-engineering-hub is an agents/LLMs hub with no documented isolation or provenance controls. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub content is copied into next-ai-draw-io prompts or MCP inputs, instruction-following can be hijacked.
IF next-ai-draw-io parses untrusted text from ai-engineering-hub as commands, prompt injection is possible.
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter and quote untrusted text before passing it between agents.
Add a manual review step before any MCP action.
Disable automatic execution of instructions extracted from documents.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all cross-agent inputs.
requires-engineering: sandbox MCP tool calls behind allowlists.

B_data_leakage.rationale: next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress, browser use, MCP, and handles API keys plus files; that creates a direct exfiltration path for content it processes. ai-engineering-hub has no documented egress, but the pair still exposes shared content to a third-party-capable agent by default. The blast radius includes documents and secrets, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub outputs are passed into next-ai-draw-io, those contents can be sent to external model APIs.
IF API keys or sensitive documents are present in next-ai-draw-io context, they may leave the local environment via its documented API calls.
mitigations: Do not pass secrets into next-ai-draw-io sessions.
Restrict next-ai-draw-io to a local-only model endpoint.
Separate workspaces so shared files are not visible to both agents.
Rotate any API keys used by next-ai-draw-io after testing.
requires-engineering: enforce outbound network allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ai-engineering-hub is a repository of agents/LLMs content, while next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances and writes diagrams/files. If both are pointed at the same workspace, they can race on shared artifacts even without explicit locking. The conflict is plausible but not proven from the docs, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file overwrites or stale reads can occur.
IF next-ai-draw-io runs multiple instances against shared files, concurrent edits can conflict.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent.
Use read-only mounts for ai-engineering-hub content.
Serialize edits with a simple manual lock file.
Check in changes one agent at a time.
requires-engineering: add filesystem locking or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io is explicitly AI-assisted and uses natural-language commands, so it may act on upstream content without strong verification. ai-engineering-hub can supply agent patterns or prompts that next-ai-draw-io renders into diagrams or actions. That creates a default pathway from one agent’s output into the other’s downstream behavior, with high risk of propagated mistakes.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub output is treated as authoritative input, next-ai-draw-io may propagate incorrect facts into diagrams or actions.
IF next-ai-draw-io auto-generates artifacts from upstream text, errors can cascade into saved work products.
mitigations: Require human verification before saving generated artifacts.
Cross-check any factual claims against a second source.
Keep ai-engineering-hub outputs as drafts only.
Add a checklist for citations and assumptions.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: next-ai-draw-io explicitly handles API keys and multiple document types, while ai-engineering-hub is an open-source agent hub with no documented retention or residency controls. The pair can therefore mix sensitive operational data with an externally connected service, but the residency/compliance mismatch is not directly evidenced, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through next-ai-draw-io, retention and third-party API exposure become compliance-relevant.
IF ai-engineering-hub content includes policy-sensitive material, it may be copied into a service with undocumented retention controls.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in next-ai-draw-io.
Review the service’s retention policy before use.
Use synthetic or redacted documents for testing.
Keep API keys out of shared workspaces.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention guarantees.
